conventions.convention: Alphabets are finite and nonempty, blocklengths satisfy n ≥ 1, and n-types are attainable empirical vectors with integer counts summing to n.
Entropy uses natural logarithms; zero entropy summands are omitted. D(q||p) is directional and equals +∞ when q assigns positive mass to a zero coordinate of p.
Product masses and event probabilities are finite sums on the full power-set sigma-algebra of the word space.
Sanov interior and closure are taken in the topology of Δ(supp(p)), induced by the ℓ¹ norm; inf ∅ = +∞ and ln 0 = −∞.
The Bernoulli threshold satisfies p ∈ [0,1) and a ∈ (p,1]; its attainable lower-bound type is ceil(na)/n. AC is assumed only for the imported Hoeffding comparison.

load_bearing.statement: Let A be a finite alphabet of size k ≥ 1, let n ≥ 1, and let q ∈ P_n(A). With natural logarithms, (n+1)^{−(k−1)}e^{nH(q)} ≤ |T_q| ≤ e^{nH(q)}.
For a finite alphabet of size k ≥ 1, a probability vector p, and q ∈ P_n(A), (n+1)^{−(k−1)}e^{−nD(q||p)} ≤ p^{⊗n}(T_q) ≤ e^{−nD(q||p)}, with e^{−n·∞} := 0 when q is not supported on p.

For a finite nonempty alphabet A, a probability vector p, and n ≥ 1, the finite mass assignment p^{⊗n} is a probability law on A^n, and its coordinate maps are independent random elements, each with law p.
Let A be finite and let p be a probability vector with p(a) > 0 for every a ∈ A. Then q ↦ D(q||p) is finite and continuous on Δ(A).
For a finite nonempty alphabet A with k = |A| ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, the type classes form a disjoint partition of A^n and |P_n(A)| ≤ (n+1)^{k−1}.
For any probability vector q on a finite nonempty alphabet of size k and every n ≥ 1, there is an n-type q_n with ||q_n−q||₁ ≤ k/n.

For a finite-alphabet probability vector p, S = supp(p), and any Γ ⊆ Δ(S), the normalized log event probabilities have liminf at least −inf over Γ° of D(q||p), and limsup at most −inf over closure(Γ) of D(q||p). The finite upper bound is (n+1)^{|S|−1} exp(−n inf over closure(Γ) D(q||p)); equal infima give the limit.

seams_checked.note: Natural-log units and support conventions agree. Actual proofs use the published finite entropy/divergence definition and do not import stronger conditional-information assertions.
This is a contextual page prerequisite. The page explicitly confines its arguments to finite product laws; no general kernel, conditioning, or measure-theoretic information theorem is invoked.
